title: 3.2.12 Lab: an Early-Return Guard Clause
description: Write a function whose first check returns early when the input is invalid, so the valid path runs without an else. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Define the function
steps.instructions: Define a function called divide that takes two parameters, a and b.

steps.title: Guard against the bad input first
steps.instructions: At the very top of the function, write an if that checks for a bad value of b, such as b equal to 0. Inside that if, return a message immediately. That early return is the guard: it ends the call before the rest of the body runs.

steps.title: Return the good result without an else
steps.instructions: After the guard, return a divided by b. Because the early return already handled the bad case, no else is needed here.

steps.title: Call it on both paths
steps.instructions: Call divide with a valid pair and with the bad value, and use console.log to print both results so you can see the guard fire.
